task.subject: Fix dual-option arbitration to respect explicit defaults

winning_diff:
--- a/src/click/core.py
+++ b/src/click/core.py
@@ -1992,7 +1992,12 @@ class Parameter(ABC):
         self.expose_value = expose_value
         self.default: t.Any | t.Callable[[], t.Any] | None = default
+        # Track whether the default was explicitly provided by the user, as
+        # opposed to an auto-derived default assigned later (e.g. ``False``
+        # for boolean flags). Used to arbitrate between competing parameters
+        # that share the same variable name.
+        self._explicit_default: bool = default is not UNSET
         self.is_eager = is_eager
         self.metavar = metavar
         self.envvar = envvar
@@ -2335,7 +2340,10 @@ class Parameter(ABC):
 
         :meta private:
         """
+        # Remember the source of a value previously stored under this name by
+        # a competing parameter, before it is updated below.
+        previous_source = ctx.get_parameter_source(self.name)
+
         with augment_usage_errors(ctx, param=self):
             value, source = self.consume_value(ctx, opts)
 
@@ -2382,12 +2390,21 @@ class Parameter(ABC):
                 value = UNSET
 
         # Add parameter's value to the context.
-        if (
-            self.expose_value
+        if self.expose_value and (
             # We skip adding the value if it was previously set by another parameter
             # targeting the same variable name. This prevents parameters competing for
             # the same name to override each other.
-            and (self.name not in ctx.params or ctx.params[self.name] is UNSET)
-        ):
+            self.name not in ctx.params
+            or ctx.params[self.name] is UNSET
+            or (
+                # An explicit default beats an auto-derived default produced by
+                # a competing parameter sharing the same name, such as the
+                # ``False`` default auto-assigned to boolean flags. When several
+                # competing parameters declare an explicit default, the last one
+                # wins. Command line input, environment variables, and the
+                # default map always win over parameter defaults.
+                source is ParameterSource.DEFAULT
+                and previous_source is ParameterSource.DEFAULT
+                and self._explicit_default
+            )
+        ):
             ctx.params[self.name] = value
 
         return value, args
